questions.question: A healthcare company must keep patient data inside Germany by law and has most users in Germany. Which factor should drive the Region choice first?
options: The Region with the most services
The Region with the most edge locations
questions.explanation: Legal data residency is a hard requirement, so compliance decides first; price, service count and edge-location count only matter among compliant Regions.

questions.question: An application runs on instances in a single data center and must survive the loss of that facility while staying in one Region. What should the architect use?
options: Multiple Availability Zones in the Region
A larger instance in the same data center
questions.explanation: AZs are isolated data centers within a Region, so spreading across them survives a facility loss; edge locations only cache content, a second Region is beyond the requirement, and a larger instance shares the same failure.

questions.question: A team plans to use a service launched last month in us-east-1 from a smaller Region. What must they verify first?
options: That the service is available in the target Region
That the Region has exactly six AZs
That IAM users exist in that Region
That the Region has an edge location
questions.explanation: New services and features are not in every Region, so availability must be checked; AZ count, IAM (global) and edge locations do not decide whether the service exists there.

questions.question: Users worldwide complain about slow downloads of static images served from one Region. Which part of the global infrastructure addresses this?
questions.explanation: Edge locations deliver content close to users with lower latency; more AZs or cheaper Regions do not move content closer, and IAM roles are unrelated to latency.

questions.question: Which identifier names an Availability Zone rather than a Region?
questions.explanation: Appending a letter (ap-southeast-2b) identifies an AZ; the other three are Region names.

questions.question: An engineer creates an IAM user while the console is set to eu-west-3. In which Regions can that user sign in?
options: All Regions, because IAM is global
Only Regions with the same AZ count
questions.explanation: IAM is a global service, so users are not tied to a Region; the other options wrongly treat IAM as Region-scoped.

questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: CloudFront is global; EC2 and Lambda are Region-scoped and Route 53 is global, so the other pairings are reversed.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of Availability Zones in an AWS Region?
questions.explanation: Regions have a minimum of 3 AZs (usually 3, at most 6); 1 and 2 are below the minimum and 6 is the maximum.
